headline: High-risk default web UI can exfiltrate sensitive context and drive unsafe actions when paired with a networked, tool-using agent; the course agent itself is non-runnable but the pair still creates interaction risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, MCP, and web content, so prompt injection is plausible if it renders attacker-controlled text; data-engineering-zoomcamp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it is not itself an injection source. The pair risk comes from open-webui bridging untrusted content into a chat/tool loop, with uncertainty about exact parsing behavior, so I choose medium.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to an MCP/OpenAPI tool server that returns attacker-controlled text
IF a user pastes or uploads course material into open-webui and then asks it to follow embedded instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP/OpenAPI tools for untrusted sources
Use a separate workspace for imported documents
Add a prompt-injection warning banner for file/web content
Restrict tool outputs to structured JSON where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, files, persistent memory, and broad network egress, while data-engineering-zoomcamp is a repository/course artifact that may be copied into the UI. If sensitive notes or files are loaded into open-webui, its default third-party API and search integrations can leak them; the course agent adds a plausible source of copied content, so the pair is high.
conditions: IF files or notes from the course repo are imported into open-webui
IF open-webui is configured with external APIs, search, or cloud-backed tools
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of open-webui
Disable external search and cloud APIs
Use offline mode and local-only models
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: data-engineering-zoomcamp is not runnable and has no write or network permissions, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. open-webui can write local files and use mounted volumes, but the pair lacks a shared writable surface in the profiles, so direct conflict is limited and likely requires unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted data volume
IF open-webui is used to edit files that the course repo also modifies
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Mount the course repo read-only
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Document ownership of any shared volume
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared mounts

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on model outputs through tools, plugins, and function calling, so if it treats course-derived text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. data-engineering-zoomcamp is a static course repo, not a verifier, so the main risk is open-webui amplifying unverified content rather than the pair causing direct harm by default.
conditions: IF open-webui is configured to execute tools based on generated answers
IF course content is copied into open-webui without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution
Disable autonomous action tools
Ask open-webui to cite sources before acting
Use a verification checklist for course-derived claims
requires-engineering: add approval gates for side-effecting actions

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, usage analytics, and files, which can create retention and residency issues if course materials or user data are loaded into it. data-engineering-zoomcamp is open-source and not itself a compliance boundary, so the compliance concern is the web UI's handling of imported data and logs.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui
IF analytics or persistent memory are enabled for that data
mitigations: Do not load regulated data into the UI
Disable analytics and persistent memory
Review retention settings before use
Keep deployments in the required region
requires-engineering: implement data-class-specific retention controls
